headline: Isaias is a 70% shot the National Hurricane Center posts an advisory of at least 111 mph by 12:00 UTC 10 October
deck: A Tropical Cyclone Update puts Isaias at 120 mph; Intermediate Advisory 11A listed 110. 70% the National Hurricane Center posts at least 111 mph by 12:00 UTC 10 October.
body: An Iowa Environmental Mesonet copy headed "Hurricane Isaias Tropical Cyclone Update" says just-received data from an Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that Isaias has strengthened to a major hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph. [E20][E18]

The National Hurricane Center's Hurricane Isaias Intermediate Advisory Number 11A, marked Corrected, listed maximum sustained winds near 110 mph, from Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft data. [E21][E19]
At the 10 p.m. CDT update, maximum sustained winds had increased to near 105 mph with higher gusts, still a Category 2 storm. [E6][E10]
The center was located near latitude 25.4 North, longitude 88.4 West at 10 p.m. CDT (0300 UTC). [E2]
This paper's 8 October file had the storm heading for the U.S. northern Gulf Coast at 80 mph. [E17]
The 10 p.m. CDT bulletin estimated the minimum central pressure at 969 mb. [E9][E13]
Isaias is moving toward the northeast near 14 mph. [E3]
A turn toward the north is expected on Friday. [E4]

On the forecast track, Isaias is expected to approach the U.S. northern Gulf Coast on Friday and make landfall within the warning area late Friday or early Saturday, between the Mississippi coast and the western Florida panhandle. [E5][E16]
Isaias could briefly become a major hurricane early Friday. [E7]
Although some weakening is forecast thereafter, Isaias will remain a dangerous hurricane as it approaches the northern Gulf Coast late Friday. [E8]
Projections in the 10 p.m. CDT update put Isaias' maximum sustained winds at 110 mph by 5 a.m. on 9 October. [E11]
A Category 3 storm, which is considered a major hurricane, has sustained winds of at least 111 mph. [E12]
Emergency managers have authorized calling up to 500 Georgia National Guard troops if conditions worsen. [E14]
The State Operations Center will shift to a Level 1 full activation on Friday at 1 p.m. [E15]

**The desk's reading.** There is a 70% probability that the National Hurricane Center posts, by 12:00 UTC on 10 October 2026, an advisory with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 mph for Hurricane Isaias at or before northern-Gulf landfall. The start is this paper's 8 October file: a strong hurricane at the coast, with no major-hurricane language. The jump to Category 2, and KNOE's statement that Isaias could briefly become a major hurricane early Friday, moved the probability up. The Iowa Environmental Mesonet copy headed Hurricane Isaias Tropical Cyclone Update at 120 mph moves it further up; Hurricane Isaias Intermediate Advisory Number 11A, marked Corrected, at 110 mph, and the 10 p.m. CDT projection just under the line for 5 a.m., hold it down. The 70% is the posted-advisory call. The storm itself reaching 111 mph is 74%. The no-post path — no such advisory on the board by 12:00 UTC even if the storm has crossed the line — is 4%, and it settles no. The strongest competing reading is that Hurricane Isaias Intermediate Advisory Number 11A, marked Corrected, is the numbered product that counts, that 110 mph is the official intensity, and that the Hurricane Isaias Tropical Cyclone Update does not settle the call, so the path still peaks below the line and then weakens. An advisory at or above that line would move the probability up; repeated advisories below it into the landfall window, or silence through 12:00 UTC, would move it down.

**The next test.** The National Hurricane Center posts, by 12:00 UTC on 10 October 2026, an advisory with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 mph for Hurricane Isaias, at or before northern-Gulf landfall. That post confirms the brief-major window was used. Landfall, or a last pre-landfall advisory, still below that line with no advisory at or above it in between confirms the peak-and-weaken path. No such advisory posted by 12:00 UTC settles no, including if the storm itself has already reached that strength.

confidence.label: Yes if the National Hurricane Center posts, by 12:00 UTC on 10 October 2026, an advisory with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 mph for Hurricane Isaias at or before northern-Gulf landfall; no if no such advisory is posted by that deadline.

flashpoint.note: A Tropical Cyclone Update put Isaias at 120 mph. Intermediate Advisory 11A listed 110 mph.

dissent.argument: Start is this paper's 8 October file: 80 mph, no major-hurricane language, a strong storm headed for the northern Gulf. The 105 mph Category 2 print at the 10 p.m. CDT update and KNOE's line that Isaias could briefly become a major hurricane early Friday moved the probability up. The Iowa Mesonet header names Tropical Cyclone Update with 120 mph recon, which moves it further — aircraft data saying the storm has already crossed 111. What should keep the posted-advisory call off 70% is Intermediate Advisory Number 11A, marked Corrected, still at 110 mph from the same class of aircraft data, one bin below the line. A Tropical Cyclone Update is not a numbered advisory and does not settle the label; 11A is still the intensity on the board. The 10 p.m. CDT projection of 110 mph by 5 a.m. and the weakening forecast after that window remain the official path. I put the storm itself at 0.62 of reaching 111 mph. The 4% no-post haircut is fair, so the posted-advisory call is 0.58. Settlement stays the same: an NHC advisory of at least 111 mph by 12:00 UTC on 10 October, at or before northern-Gulf landfall; no if none is posted by then. A numbered advisory at or above 111 would move me up; a second numbered product still at 110, or a TCU retraction, would move me down.
